input.story: I bought a washing machine for 28000 in January 2024 and it stopped working in February 2024. The company never fixed it despite many calls. Can I file a consumer case now?

output.masked_story: I bought a washing machine for 28000 in January 2024 and it stopped working in February 2024. The company never fixed it despite many calls. Can I file a consumer case now?

case.problem_subtype: defective product not repaired or replaced
case.summary: The user purchased a washing machine for 28000 in January 2024 which stopped working in February 2024. Despite multiple calls, the company failed to repair or replace it.
case.user_goal: File a consumer case to get a refund or replacement

timeline.event: Washing machine stopped working and company failed to fix it despite calls

evidence_missing: service request numbers or call logs
follow_up_questions: Which Indian state are you currently living in?
Do you have the purchase invoice and warranty card for the washing machine?
Did you receive any written response or job sheet from the service center when you raised complaints?

flags.message: The problem started about 2.9 years ago. The usual time limit for this kind of claim is around 2 years - it may be expired or about to expire. See a lawyer quickly.

notes: A Consumer Commission can also award compensation and litigation costs - we don't estimate that figure; it depends on the case.
Interest on delayed money may be claimable; the rate is for a lawyer/court to decide, so we don't add it here.

assessment.where_you_stand: You purchased a washing machine for Rs 28,000 in January 2024 which stopped working in February 2024, and the company failed to repair or replace it. Under the law, a defective product or failure to provide service is considered a deficiency [KB:cpa_consumer_def], [KB:src_cpa_2019_83]. However, a red flag has been raised regarding the time limit for filing a complaint [KB:cpa_limitation], [KB:src_cpa_2019_69], and you are currently missing essential proof like the purchase invoice and warranty card. Because of the potential time limit issue and missing documents, you should consult a lawyer before proceeding.

options.title: Contact National Consumer Helpline [KB:forum_nch]
options.what_to_do: Call 1915 or file a pre-litigation complaint on the National Consumer Helpline [KB:forum_nch] website to try and get a resolution from the company without a formal case.
needs: Any payment proof, dealer name, and call details

options.title: Consult a Lawyer
options.what_to_do: Speak with a legal professional to evaluate if your complaint is within the limitation period and how to proceed without an invoice.

options.title: File a Consumer Complaint on e-Jagriti [KB:forum_ejagriti]
options.what_to_do: If pre-litigation steps fail and a lawyer confirms you can proceed, file a formal complaint online on the e-Jagriti [KB:forum_ejagriti] portal.
options.cost: free (for claims up to Rs 5 lakh)
needs: Purchase proof, complaint history, ID proof

proof_tips: Check your bank or UPI statements from January 2024 to find proof of the Rs 28,000 payment to the seller
Contact the dealer or store where you bought the machine to request a duplicate purchase invoice
Gather any phone logs, emails, or text messages showing your attempts to contact the company for repairs
what_i_dont_know: Whether the exact limitation period has expired based on the exact dates of your last communication with the company
If the dealer can trace your purchase history to issue a replacement invoice
assessment.needs_lawyer_reason: A red flag was raised regarding the time limit for filing a consumer claim, and you lack key documents like the purchase invoice. A lawyer should review your case before you take further action.
assessment.reply: Because our system flagged a potential time limit issue regarding your consumer complaint, and you are currently missing your purchase invoice and warranty card, it is best to be cautious. Under consumer laws, you generally have a two-year window from when the problem arose to file a formal complaint [KB:cpa_limitation], [KB:src_cpa_2019_69], though a defective product is considered a deficiency in service [KB:cpa_consumer_def], [KB:src_cpa_2019_83]. Your first step should be gathering alternative proof, such as checking your bank statement from January 2024 for the Rs 28,000 transaction and contacting the store for a duplicate invoice. You can also try reaching out to the National Consumer Helpline for pre-litigation assistance [KB:forum_nch]. Because of the timeline concerns and missing paperwork, consulting a lawyer or legal aid before taking formal legal action is strongly advised [KB:lsa_s12_legal_aid]. Do you have any bank statements or SMS alerts from the time of purchase that can help prove when you bought the machine?
